claim.quote: Observation of a neutrino burst from the supernova SN1987A

date.note: The neutrino burst itself was recorded 23 February 1987; the paper was published in Phys. Rev. Lett. 58, 1490 (April 1987).
date.quote: A neutrino burst was observed in the Kamiokande II detector on 23 February, 7:35:35 UT (+-1 min) during a time interval of 13 sec.

key_value_text.quote: A neutrino burst was observed in the Kamiokande II detector on 23 February, 7:35:35 UT (+-1 min) during a time interval of 13 sec.
key_value_text.value: A neutrino burst of 13-second duration observed in the Kamiokande-II detector on 23 February 1987, 7:35:35 UT (+/- 1 min).

name: Kamiokande-II observation of SN 1987A neutrinos

official_url.note: No official experiment result page carries a URL for this 1987 paper in the sources fetched; only the journal DOI record is available.

summary.plain: In February 1987 the Kamiokande detector caught a short burst of neutrinos from a star exploding in a nearby galaxy - the first time humans had ever detected neutrinos from any star other than our own Sun.
summary.technical: Kamiokande-II recorded a 13-second burst of neutrino events on 23 February 1987, 7:35:35 UT, coincident with the optical detection of supernova SN 1987A in the Large Magellanic Cloud, confirming core-collapse supernova neutrino emission and opening neutrino astronomy of transient sources.

title: Observation of a neutrino burst from the supernova SN1987A
why_it_matters: The first (and to date only) detection of neutrinos from a supernova outside the Solar System, confirming core-collapse theory and founding supernova/multimessenger neutrino astronomy; part of the work recognised by the 2002 Nobel Prize in Physics to Masatoshi Koshiba.
